questions.q: In query federation with Snowflake, which system's compute answers the query?
options: Snowflake's own compute
The end user's browser
Only a Salesforce Apex trigger
No compute is used
questions.explain: Data 360 sends the query to Snowflake, which runs it on its own compute. Warehouse cost therefore lands on the Snowflake side.

questions.q: How does file federation differ from query federation?
options: It copies all Snowflake data into Salesforce objects nightly
It only works for CSV uploads
Data 360 reads the underlying files directly instead of using Snowflake compute, with stricter prerequisites such as Iceberg tables
It requires no Snowflake account
questions.explain: File federation reads storage directly, avoiding external compute, but it depends on supported table formats and cloud setups.

questions.q: What does zero-copy data sharing out to Snowflake accomplish?
options: It deletes CRM data after each query
It exports a monthly PDF report
It replaces Snowflake with Salesforce
It makes Data 360 data accessible to Snowflake users without an outbound ETL job
questions.explain: Salesforce describes sharing as making Data 360 insights available to platforms like Snowflake without building an outbound ETL process.

questions.q: You need daily snapshots of Opportunity history for trend analysis. Which approach fits best?
options: Live query federation only, because it stores history automatically
Load Salesforce objects into Snowflake on a schedule and model them there
Rely on file uploads from the browser
Nothing can provide history
questions.explain: Federation shows current state. Snapshots and history need a load, such as an extract-and-load pipeline modeled with dbt.

questions.q: Which security practice does the lesson recommend for the Snowflake connection?
options: Use an administrator's personal account
Share one password across the whole team
Grant every role full access to be safe
Use a least-privilege Snowflake role and a service identity
questions.explain: A dedicated service identity with only the access it needs limits risk and makes usage easier to audit.
